sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer systems designed to understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of artificial intelligence called neural networks, specifically transformer models, and are trained on vast amounts of text data.

sections.title: How Do LLMs Process Text?
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or even characters. These tokens are then transformed into embeddings, which are mathematical representations that capture the meanings and relationships between words.

sections.title: The Role of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the instructions or questions we give to LLMs to guide their responses. The way we phrase these prompts can greatly influence the quality and relevance of the answers, making prompt design an important skill.

sections.title: Improving LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like prompt engineering help customize how LLMs respond by providing clear and structured instructions. Tools that automatically generate prompts can enhance performance, especially in complex reasoning tasks, by ensuring the model follows a logical thought process.

sections.title: Challenges with LLMs
sections.body: Despite their capabilities, LLMs can produce inaccurate or fabricated information, known as hallucinations. This is why careful prompt design and structured reasoning are essential, especially in educational settings where reliable answers are crucial.
